title: Conditions of the Master Grain Marketing Agreement: Closing Out Bushels Already Sold
content:
A member on Grain Marketing Contracts who will not deliver the bushels they sold buys the contract out rather than walking away from it.

**1. Notice.** Notice must reach the desk no later than the programme's notice window before the delivery window closes.

**2. Withdrawal before countersigning.** On programmes that allow it, an application may still be withdrawn at no cost at all while it is in applied standing and has not been countersigned.

**3. How the charge is collected.** The buyout is drawn as a deduction on the member's next settlement statement, and where there is no settlement to draw it on it is invoiced to the member's crop input account.

**4. Where the window closes instead.** Where the window closes with bushels still owed and no buyout arranged the contract goes to default instead, which carries the default penalty per bushel on top of the same market loss, so buying out early is always the cheaper of the two.

## Clauses no longer in force

Three clauses of these conditions are **no longer in force** and are carried here only so that no reader applies them:

> "The member has signed a buyout instruction and the grain desk has registered it before the contract is cancelled; a telephone call saying the crop failed starts the conversation but does not cancel anything."

> "The buyout price is the market loss on the undelivered bushels, being the amount by which the replacement bid on the day of cancellation exceeds the contract price, multiplied by the programme's loss multiplier and never less than zero, plus the programme's flat administrative fee."

> "Where the market has fallen the loss is zero and only the administrative fee is charged; the cooperative does not pay the member the difference."

The notice window, the free withdrawal before countersigning, the collection route and the default consequence all stand as written above.
